author: Bryanna Moore
title: Black cardiology group launches campaign to tackle 'silent crisis' in cardiology deserts - NewsBreak
text: BATON ROUGE, La. ( Louisiana First ) — As Louisiana faces another summer of dangerous heat, doctors say the threat of heart attacks is growing, especially in rural communities where access to care is nearly nonexistent. That’s why the Association of Black Cardiologists (ABC) is launching a new nationwide campaign aimed at preventing cardiovascular emergencies before they start. “The impetus is on us to make sure that these heart attacks don’t happen,” said Dr. Paul Underwood, an ABC board member. “But everyone is not getting the message, and certainly not everyone is taking action to make sure that’s what actually happens.” The group’s “Cardiology Deserts” campaign targets the estimated 44 million people in the U.S. who live without adequate access to cardiovascular care. Many of those patients are concentrated in the south, including parishes in Louisiana with no full-time cardiologists. “And it seems that those areas are where we’re seeing the highest cardiovascular mortality,” Underwood said. The campaign’s first phase is an 18-month initiative focusing on education and prevention. It will provide cholesterol screenings, health talks, and resources to help underserved communities identify and manage heart disease risk factors. The effort will span both rural areas and urban neighborhoods that lack specialist care. “We’re actually providing free LDL-C testing, either during events like health fairs, or we’ll offer an option where people can scan a QR code and get a free at-home testing kit,” Underwood said. The goal, he added, is to empower people to take control of their heart health, especially by discussing cholesterol levels and other key indicators with their healthcare providers.
